question: Which of the following non-metals is liquid at room temperature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bromine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bromine is the only non-metal that is liquid at room temperature.
 
• It is a reddish-brown element that evaporates easily to form a similarly colored gas.
 
• Bromine is found in nature primarily in the form of bromide salts in the Earth's crust and seawater.
 
• It has a melting point of -7.2°C and a boiling point of 58.8°C, making it liquid between these temperatures under standard conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Properties of Bromine:**

 
 
• Bromine is highly reactive and is a member of the halogen group in the periodic table.
 
• It is toxic and causes irritation to the skin, eyes, and respiratory system.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Bromine:**
 
 
• Bromine compounds are used in fire retardants, water purification, and as intermediates in the manufacture of organic chemicals.
 
• It is also used in photography and the production of dyes and pharmaceuticals.
 
 
 
• **Occurrence:**
 
 
• Bromine is the 64th most abundant element in Earth's crust and is found in seawater at a concentration of about 65 parts per million.
 
• It is extracted from brine pools and salt lakes.
 
 
 
• **Safety Measures:**
 
 
• Due to its toxicity, bromine must be handled with care, using appropriate safety equipment and ventilation.
 
• Exposure to bromine vapors can be harmful, so it is important to have proper containment and protective measures in place.
